correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southwestern opening and initial northward-to-eastward headward corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected opening and its first bends were considered. FEP distinguishes the upper Hueque south of Cabure from the Remedios/Upipe tributary relationship, but supplies no inspected channel map assigning this southwestern opening to either branch. No local feeder name or source point is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward upper corridor and first northeastward transition
correspondence.finding: Regional prose states that Upipe is named Remedios farther upstream. This is a useful tributary lead, but does not demonstrate the selected eastward route, individual joins or the turn into its northeastward corridor. These connections remain material gaps.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward and northeastward middle corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected middle route and intervening joins are outside the acquired estuary study. FEP tributary prose alone does not establish the through-link from this corridor into the named lower Hueque. No Remedios-to-Upipe name boundary is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower approach to the Hueque floodplain
correspondence.finding: FEP describes a flat, seasonally inundated lower Hueque receiving Upipe and the convergence of Jacura and Guamure toward its floodplain. Neither the actual selected approach nor its meeting with the lower receiving course is depicted by the local estuary map; naming the basin does not complete this interval.

correspondence.component_scope: Transition into the mapped estuarine corridor
correspondence.finding: The last approach begins south of the inspected local estuary map. A portion reaches the map’s southern geographic range, but the whole transition from the unmapped upstream interval is not established. No reservoir crossing is inferred from references to the separate upper Hueque impoundment.

correspondence.component_scope: Western Hueque estuarine branch, mouth-facing reach and actual marine endpoint
correspondence.finding: Figure1 maps the western Hueque channel through the mangrove floodplain and distinguishes the eastern Curarí channel. Figure10 and the authors’ prose describe their meeting immediately before the Caribbean outlet, with a short northeastward final turn of Hueque. The selected final corridor and actual offshore endpoint correspond to this western-branch/Boca de Hueque setting at ordinary corridor scale. The schematic selected line and historical map are not asserted to have identical banks or precise tidal-channel vertices; the marine endpoint is not treated as a named river continuing offshore.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southwestern opening and west-to-east feeder
correspondence.finding: Figure 1 depicts the southern western feeder extending west of the chosen opening and east toward the central lake/junction setting. The selected opening, eastern progression and intervening joins correspond at ordinary regional scale. The feeder is not individually named in this figure.

correspondence.component_scope: Intermediate lake/junction setting and northeast turn
correspondence.finding: Figure 1 depicts the selected western feeder meeting the small lake/junction setting, followed by the northeastward connecting reach into the upper trunk. The selected route uses the southern incoming branch; the separate branch from the northwestern interior is not substituted for it. Minor waterbodies remain unnamed.

correspondence.component_scope: East-trending Alexis River trunk and Alexis Creek junction
correspondence.finding: The named Alexis River in Figure 1 follows the east-trending selected corridor. Alexis Creek is separately labeled on the northern branch joining this trunk, so that tributary name is not applied to the selected western feeder. The independent water-quality station profile locates an Alexis River monitoring reach in this same middle corridor and describes its upstream lake/stream headwaters and downstream Port Hope Simpson setting.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeast-trending lower river and transition to the estuary
correspondence.finding: Figure 1 follows the river southeast from the main junction region to the inland end of the coastal inlet west of Port Hope Simpson. The station account independently describes the downstream connection to Port Hope Simpson and an outlet on Alexis Bay. The selected route remains on this lower corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Stored inner-estuary continuation and actual eastern terminal
correspondence.finding: Figure 1 depicts a continuous elongated coastal-water passage from the lower river past the Port Hope Simpson vicinity, continuing east beyond the actual stored terminal. The complete selected terminal extension is retained as an estuarine component rather than replaced with the earlier freshwater mouth. The regional figure establishes this estuarine corridor but does not distinguish every small island-side channel.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen eastern opening and upper joining approach
correspondence.finding: The eastern start belongs to the upper Cañar geographic setting, but the independent field-site evidence does not follow this entire opening into the sampled San Pedro reach and onward joining approach. The provincial map cannot separate it sufficiently.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper southern bend and sampled San Pedro/Cañar localities
correspondence.finding: San Pedro is supported as a distinct upper reach by the author’s sampling observations. Coyoctor and La Posta sites independently carry Cañar. These site identifications do not extend one scalar name over the entire selected upper route.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Cañar valley toward the La Troncal plain
correspondence.finding: The inspected provincial and municipal compilations show the westward receiving corridor from the El Tambo/Suscal valley toward the lowland south of La Troncal, with ordinary regional continuity.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Cañar and separate diversion setting
correspondence.finding: Lower Cañar continues southwest through the Puerto Inca plain. The municipal account identifies Patul and Piedras inputs and a separate northwest diversion toward La Lagartera; the selected route follows the lower receiving corridor rather than that bypass.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual stored terminal at the coastal tidal-channel setting
correspondence.finding: Map8 follows the selected lower approach into the eastern tidal-channel network at the stored ending. The finding stops there; it does not extend the feature to an assumed open-ocean mouth.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening and long initial southward Inland Ice passage
correspondence.finding: Both actual originals place the chosen northern opening and the complete long initial southward part in Inland Ice. The regional original shows the opening below the higher interior ice contours and follows its southward approach to the first eastward turn. These are ice-surface contours and terrain observations, not mapped river channels or a natural-river hydronym.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward turn and southeastward interior-ice sequence
correspondence.finding: The entire sequence after the first eastward turn remains in mapped ice, passing west of small exposed or uncoloured inland outliers. Every short selected part, bend and intermediate join is exposed in the original cartography. No river name or surface or subglacial water continuity is established by the ice contours.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward ice passage toward A. Kornerup Land and Holmlandet
correspondence.finding: The next southward passage remains in mapped ice among increasingly frequent small nunataks and approaches the larger exposed-rock terrain west of A. Kornerup Land. The full southward approach and following southeastward bend are covered. A. Kornerup Land is a land label and does not identify a river.

correspondence.component_scope: Ice, exposed-rock and intervening inland pockets around Holmlandet
correspondence.finding: The regional original exposes the complete eastward and southward succession around Holmlandet. It depicts an ice indentation north of the bedrock, a narrow uncoloured inland corridor with blue-dotted Quaternary deposits, adjacent uncoloured water-like pockets, and the coloured rock tract before the next broad ice passage. The selected line crosses this mixed setting rather than following a separately named river depicted by the map. Geographic correspondence is complete at ordinary corridor scale; a lake-throughflow or natural-watercourse link through the rock tract is not established.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestward lower ice corridor
correspondence.finding: The subsequent southwestward sequence occupies the narrow mapped ice corridor along the eastern side of Johan Dahl Land and west of the broader Qooqqup Sermia glacier setting. The original distinguishes the coloured rock sides, intervening ice and the nearby separate Qooroq fjord. All selected parts and their joins are exposed. Neither the glacier label nor the adjacent fjord label is applied to the whole selected river group.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower ice margin and valley approach to Narsarsuaq
correspondence.finding: The complete continuation descends from the narrow ice tongue into the valley and blue-dotted Quaternary-deposit setting northeast of Narsarsuaq, then approaches the inner coastal water. The actual regional original exposes the intervening bedrock, mapped valley/channel linework, deposits and final westward turn. This supplies geographic correspondence of the lower passage; no named reach or whole-route hydraulic continuity is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected ending at the Narsarsuaq-side fjord head
correspondence.finding: The final short part and supplied ending lie in the Narsarsuaq-side head-of-Tunulliarfik setting reached from the northeastern valley. The regional original distinguishes this ending from Qooroq, the separate fjord to the east. The ending and its approach are actually covered, without extending the selection down the fjord or assigning its fjord name to a river. No exact present bank, glacier-front position or contemporary mouth condition is claimed.
